SECTION VI - ALTERNATIVES TO THE PROPOSED ACTION
6.01 General. The proposed action is described in detail in section I of this statement. Briefly, it is a hydroelectric power plant facility of 57,000 kW installed capacity (32,000 kW at minimum head) to be added to the existing Amistad Dam. The plan of improvement includes operating the existing Falcon and proposed Amistad hydropower plants as a two unit system. Falcon power is fed into a large distribution network, and Amistad power would be fed into the same network.
6.02 A study for the two plant system was performed to determine the amount of power and energy that would be developed. Two conditions were considered, one for a two unit addition to the dam on the United States side and the other condition for a two unit addition to both the United States and Mexican sides (i.e., 2 + 2). For the interim condition of adding two US units, equivalent to releases for power varying from 3,800 cfs to 4,500 cfs, there would be an overall increase of 282,400,000 kWh average annual energy consisting of 281,800,000 kWh from the new US Amistad powerhouse and 600,000 kWh from the existing Falcon powerhouse. All of the energy would be marketed to US customers. The study shows that a rather wide deviation from the average can be expected because of the long periods of dry weather experienced in the Rio Grande basin upstream from Amistad Reservoir to El Paso. No new facilities would be constructed at Falcon to gain the additional average annual energy; instead, the increase would result from the water surface in Falcon Reservoir being more constant and an energy highly higher average elevation (thus increasing the average net head on the turbines)
6.03 For the ultimate condition of adding two units to each side, equivalent to releases for power in the range of 9,000 cfs, the energy available to US customers would amount to about 58 percent of that available during interim conditions; that is, there would be about 163,300,000 kWh of new energy consisting of 161,800,000 kWh from the US Amistad powerhouse and 1,500,000 kWh from the existing Falcon powerhouse, available for sale to US customers.
6.04 Mexico has not stated when it expects to build its powerhouse. In view of the fact that this impact statement cannot address an undefined proposed action, the remaining portion of section VI, covering alternatives, will refer to the interim condition. However, the reader should bear in mind that at some time in the future, there will likely be two to four generating units added on the Mexican side, in accordance with the prior International agreements (see paragraphs 1.18-1.23).
Alternatives to the Amistad Hydroelectric Facility
6.05 General. Fast breeder nuclear reactors, large wind diven electrical generators, solar collectors, and tidal wave generators are some of the so-called "exotic" electrical power alternatives. The nuclear reactors and tidal wave generators would be very large facilities, the energy from which would be distributed over existing electrical transmission networks. Wind turbines and solar collectors could be of various sizes, ranging from units to serve an individual household up to large units to serve small towns. All of these devices are experimental and are possible long range solutions to the energy problem. At present, they are either technically in the development stage or they are not economically feasible when compared to conventional methods of electric generation.
